title: Crescent shift bridge report — evening handoff
content:
Shift window: 2026-09-18 18:00 -> 2026-09-18 23:59 UTC
Owner (this shift): Maya Chen (evening watch)
Taking over from: morning watch (Aisha P.) at 18:00 UTC
Receiving: cluster stable after morning maintenance; small burst of warm restarts during 11:30–12:00 UTC that were resolved by rolling restart.

Quick status:
- Redwood hosted API: nominal for most endpoints. Small increase in 95th latency for chat-gen between 22:05–22:35 UTC (peak 2.1s -> baseline 1.0s).
- Dedicated pools: healthy. GPU memory pressure on gpupool-3 is elevated but within alert thresholds.
- Observability: traces show increased retry count for chat-gen route; no error-rate spike beyond 0.5%

Incidents / notable events (chronological):
1) 22:10 UTC — chat-gen route transient degradation (incident ref: JIRA SRE-4123)
- Symptom: sudden spike in tail latency and user-observed slow responses (customers: a few PLG accounts reported degraded experience).
- Alerting: P95 latency alert fired for hosted-api/chat-gen; auto-incident created and paged oncall.
- Immediate triage: looked at autoscaler and pod lifecycle events — saw a burst of pod restarts on nodes in us-west2 availability set; restart reason: OOMKilled on sidecar process (metrics-proxy v0.7.2).
- Root cause hypothesis (initial): metrics-proxy regression consuming extra heap under high connection churn; triggered autoscaler to create replacement pods which took ~30–60s, causing short-lived high-latency tail.
- Actions taken:
    * Scaled out temporary extra replicas for chat-gen service (kubectl scale deployment/chat-gen -n hosted --replicas=12) — mitigated queueing pressure.
    * Rolled out previous stable metrics-proxy image (v0.7.1) to a single canary pod on gpupool-3 for validation.
    * Added a short-term HPA cooldown override to prevent cascade restarts (documented below).
- Escalation: paged infra lead Luis Romero at 22:20 UTC to validate metrics-proxy memory behavior and coordinate rollback if canary shows regressions.
- Resolution: by 22:45 UTC P95 latency returned to baseline. No customer-facing incident declared.
- Follow-ups: see 'Post-shift tasks'.

2) 20:30 UTC — minor alert: KV-cache hit ratio dip for embeddings service (no user impact).
- Observed temporary spike in cold-starts for embedding pods after a short GC storm on node-18; self-healed after 10 minutes. Logged as FYI and added to monitoring dashboard watchlist.

Operational notes and commands run (kept short for handoff):
- Checked pods: kubectl get pods -n hosted -l app=chat-gen -o wide
- Described restarted pod: kubectl describe pod chat-gen-7b6ff -n hosted -> saw OOMKilled: metrics-proxy
- Canary rollout: kubectl set image deploy/metrics-proxy metrics-proxy=registry.redwood.io/metrics-proxy:v0.7.1 -n infra-canary
- Temporary HPA cooldown change: kubectl patch hpa chat-gen -n hosted -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}}}}'

Runbook gaps observed (actionable updates to crescent runbook):
- Add a dedicated troubleshooting subsection for metrics-proxy OOM patterns (include log grep patterns, heap dump steps, and safe rollback instructions).
- Concrete HPA recommended cooldowns per service profile (chat-gen needs a 300s scaleDown stabilization by default).
- Guidance for temporary horizontal scaling during metrics-sidecar regressions (who can approve + required notification channels).

Open follow-ups (assignments):
- SRE-4123 (owner: Luis Romero) — fully revert metrics-proxy to v0.7.1 across hosted for stable rollout; do canary in eu-west1 and us-east1 next window; estimate 2h, target: 2026-09-19 02:00 UTC.
- RUNBOOK-UPDATE-27 (owner: Maya Chen) — add metrics-proxy troubleshooting notes and HPA defaults to Crescent Runbook; include playbook snippets and exact kubectl commands. Target: 2026-09-19 EOD.
- MONITOR-189 (owner: Tom Nguyen) — add a synthetic check for chat-gen P95 under short-burst connection churn to detect metrics-proxy regressions earlier. Target: 2026-09-20.

Customer communications
- No incident declared; product team suggested a short status note to customers who reported slowness explaining transient latencies and that platform is stable. Product contact: Sarah Li (product-hosted-api). I drafted a one-paragraph email and pasted it into #prod-incident for review (Slack thread link below).

Notes for next shift (urgent items first)
- Verify metrics-proxy canary logs in infra-canary namespace (search for heap growth and long GC pauses) — check logs since 22:20 UTC.
- Confirm whether Luis completes the host-wide revert and update JIRA SRE-4123 with rollback PR link.
- Monitor gpupool-3 memory pressure and eviction counts; if evictions increase, scale gpupool-3 by +1 node after consulting infra.

Non-urgent items to track
- Revisit HPA policies globally; propose a baseline stabilization window table.
- Investigate why metrics-proxy 0.7.2 slipped past staging (gap in release test coverage for connection churn).

Attachments & links (operational):
- Log slices: https://logs.redwood.ai/g/hosted/chat-gen/2026-09-18-22
- Dashboards: Hosted API P95: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/p95-chat-gen
- Slack thread (customer reports): https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0ABCDEF1/p1695073320000000

Immediate handoff summary (for oncoming night watch):
- Current system state: stable; canary running metrics-proxy v0.7.1 with no anomalies so far.
- Active follow-ups: SRE-4123 (metrics-proxy revert); MONITOR-189; RUNBOOK-UPDATE-27.
- Suggested first 30 mins for next oncall: validate canary logs, verify HPA cooling still applied, confirm no new OOMs on gpupool-3.

Questions / decisions needed from next oncall or on-call lead:
- If canary in eu-west1 shows problems, do we rollback global or throttle traffic via routing policy? (Luis to advise).
- Approve HPA stabilization defaults for chat-gen (proposal in RUNBOOK-UPDATE-27).

Signed off: Maya Chen (evening watch)
Contact: maya@redwood.ai, Pager: +1-555-0103

End of report.
